links.outcome: Contextual relevance, clinical appropriateness, and practical usability of counseling responses (human evaluation across five metrics; BERTScore F1 and SBERT cosine similarity)
links.effect: KG-based approaches consistently improved contextual relevance, clinical appropriateness, and practical usability compared to RAG alone; no numeric values reported in the abstract
links.tradeoff: The KG was constructed manually and clinically validated with contributions from multidisciplinary people, implying a curation burden; no cost or latency figures reported.
links.quote: The results show that KG-based approaches consistently improve contextual relevance, clinical appropriateness, and practical usability compared to RAG alone, demonstrating that structured, expert-validated knowledge plays a critical role in addressing LLMs limitations in counseling tasks.

design_hint: retrieval grounding with clinically validated knowledge graph vs RAG
